To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of harmonically excited modes in a resonant cavity with a Josephson point contact can be very large and the frequencies of the excited harmonics can be in the optical band.
the frequency of oscillations of the current through a superconducting weak link is a function of the magnetic flux through the link.
a superconductor–superconductor weak link in the presence of an external microwave field can operate under nonequilibrium, high-frequency, conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of superconducting point contact, which is capable of operating in a nonequilibrium mode.
the study of superconducting weak-link structures for the generation of high-frequency radiation.
the development of a theory for the operation of a superconductivity point junction in a resonator as a generator of high-frequency electromagnetic radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Josephson junctions and the superconducting resonators are very promising for the generation of submillimeter radiation.
a Josephson junction is not a good candidate for frequency multiplication.
a superconducting weak link is a promising element for use as a nonlinear device in the microwave range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Josephson junction can be used as a frequency multiplier.
a superconducting junction is an ideal element for frequency multiplication, especially if the junction is operated in a regime where the Josephson current is strongly suppressed.
we have shown the possibility of frequency multiplication in a resonant circuit by using the nonlinear properties of a superconductive junction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of the output signal is not a simple multiple of the frequency of the input signal, and the output signal can be generated at any frequency within a certain band.
the frequency multiplication of the Josephson junction can be used in a number of applications, including in the generation of submillimeter waves.
